headline: Record quarter across the board; full-year guidance raised
summary_short: Revenue rose 11.8% year over year to $4.41 billion and net income grew 21.1% to $753 million, as United Rentals raised its full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance.
summary_long: Revenue reached $4.41B (+11.8% y/y), driven by 12.7% rental-revenue growth as average fleet (OEC) grew 7.1% y/y and fleet productivity rose 3.4%. Net income was $753M (+21.1% y/y, 17.1% margin), including a $37M after-tax gain on the scaffolding-business sale; excluding it, net margin still rose 40bp y/y on higher rental gross margin. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.06B (+13.6% y/y); excluding the gain, adjusted EBITDA margin fell 40bp as specialty-segment mix shifted toward lower-margin ancillary and re-rent revenue, partly offset by lower labor costs. United Rentals raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue ($17.5-17.8B) and adjusted EBITDA ($7.975-8.125B). Net leverage was 1.8x with $3.0B total liquidity at quarter-end.

drivers.explanation: Rental revenue grew 12.7% y/y on 7.1% average-fleet (OEC) growth and 3.4% fleet-productivity gains, plus a 3.7pt contribution from ancillary and re-rent revenue.
General Rentals segment gross margin rose 70bp y/y on lower depreciation as a % of revenue; Specialty Rentals margin fell 140bp on mix shift toward lower-margin ancillary/re-rent revenue.
Includes a $37M after-tax ($0.58/share) gain on the sale of part of the scaffolding business; excluding that gain, net margin still rose 40bp y/y on higher rental gross margin.
Includes the $0.58/share after-tax gain on the scaffolding-business sale disclosed for net income above; diluted share count fell to 62.6M from 64.9M a year ago on continued buybacks.

Excluding the scaffolding-sale gain, adjusted EBITDA margin fell 40bp y/y as specialty-segment mix shifted toward lower-margin ancillary and re-rent revenue, partly offset by lower labor and benefits costs as a % of revenue.
